title: Interview Posters
description: A constant output project where I made posters every week based off of interviews with my peers, inspired by a previous project I attempted in high school.
overlayHTML:
Interview Posters



Sep 2024 - Dec 2024


We were challenged to develop a self directed creative project which we would work on weekly in order to improve our creative processes in our Ideation and Prototyping class. I decided to revamp a project I'd attempted in high school. The project was called "My Story".



But this proved to be difficult to maintain on top of AP Art classwork as the portfolio deadline approached. So when presented with the Constant Outpute project I decided to attempt this project once more on a more manageable scale. Instead of making full blown artworks, I chose to make posters in order to learn Adobe Illustrator based off of a similar interview I would take of my peers. I changed the questions slightly instead of just focusing on change, geared more towards the transition from childhood to college. All of these posters' elements are hand-drawn! I started off in Canva because that was what I was most comfortable with. However once I started getting more comfortable with Illustrator in my Visual Foundations class, I transitioned to using Illustrator fully. Below are some of my favorite posters!

title: Rogue Aerospace Merchandise
description: A Vertically Integrated Project (VIP) for which I created various designs for stickers, clothing, made stoles and iterated on new logos for.
overlayHTML:
Rogue Aerospace Design


Rogue Aerospace Final Presentation by Srividhya Chandramouleeswaran
stickers I drew for Rogue

Jan 2025- Present


Rogue Aerospace is part of NYU’s Vertically Integrated Projects (VIP) at the Brooklyn campus of the NYU Tandon School of Engineering. As a member of the Operations team last semester, I was working on merchandise design. Unfortunately, since we weren't selected for the Alabama competition in the school year, my designs haven't seen print at the moment. Rogue heads challenged me to create merchandise for them that did not rely on their "Rats go Rogue" theme they had been using for the past few years.


initial back of t-shirt and front of tshirt logo respectively

I studied their past t-shirt designs to inform my decisions on how to design both the stickers and the merchandise. I saw both a lot of simple geometric designs as well as ones that were extremely intricate and bold. I used both illustrator and Procreate to design the stickers, using Pinterest to help me find references for rocket designs. Since just drawing rockets wasn't as visually appealing, I tried to combine astronaut characters, the moon, the NYU torch, and rockets in future iterations. I made sure to utilize line thickness to my advantage to create visual appeal since the designs for clothing could not have their own colors. Students generally wore black/ white on purple or white on black and vice versa

revised tshirt backs

Towards the end of the year, I was asked to help create the stoles for all the graduating seniors from scratch. Using the provided Rogue Aerospace font to create the vertical Rogue Aerospace text, the branding guide to create all the position names, and traced the rocket design in illustrator, provided to me from diagrams the lead sent me. I mocked it up on figma and spent two days at the makerspace bringing them to life by cutting them on HTV (heat transfer vinyl) and transferring them onto the satin stoles. The lead and I rn into a lot of problems but we pushed through and presented the stoles to the seniors!



I also worked on reimagining the Rogue identity and was tasked with creating new logos for Rogue. In true NYC fashion our team over the summer settled on an astro pigeon for which I iterated on
